Farm names (e.g. Haatoft, Hestdal) are residence locators, not surnames. A person who moved farms will appear under a different farm name in later records. The same individual may appear as 'Anders Monsen Haatoft' in one record and 'Anders Monsen [new farm]' in another.

The compiled extract 'Register over døpte, gifte og begravede' (FamilySearch Catalog 261335, compiled by Haarstad and Luker from Hamre kirkebok nr. 1 and 3) is the most efficient first search tool for the 1760-1800 target window — search it before browsing raw images.

A Sjeleregister (Register of Souls) covering Hamre and other Hordaland parishes exists for 1738-1811 on Digitalarkivet. This household-level clerical census falls within the target window and may place Anders and Unna in specific farm households. URL: https://www.digitalarkivet.no/en/search/sources?s=&from=&to=&format=all&archive_key=&st%5B%5D=SJEL&c%5B%5D=12
Some Meland farms belonged to Lysekloster Estate; their probate records were kept at Hardanger og Voss, not Nordhordland — search there if Nordhordland skifteprotokoller yield nothing.

The Hamre registers on Digitalarkivet are browse-only images for 1760-1800. The national indexed FamilySearch marriage collection (1468080) may include some Hamre extracts but completeness for this window is not confirmed; image browsing of the Hamre volume 1750-1857 on Digitalarkivet is necessary.

Naming pattern: the first son was typically named for the paternal grandfather, the second for the maternal grandfather. Finding baptism records for Anders and Unna's children will likely reveal the names 'Mons' and 'Halstein' as grandfathers, confirming identity of the correct couple.

The adjacent Manger prestegjeld archive burned in 1759, destroying earlier records there. The Hamre archive appears to have survived intact from 1677 onward per the Hamre Parish wiki. These are separate archives — the fire did not affect Hamre records.

Efficient research sequence: (1) Search compiled extract FamilySearch Catalog 261335; (2) search Norway Marriages 1660-1926 (coll. 1468080); (3) browse Hamre 1750-1857 images on Digitalarkivet for the marriage register section; (4) check the Sjeleregister; (5) on finding a marriage date, search baptism records for children; (6) search probate index (coll. 1661306) for estate divisions naming the family.

# Locality Guide: Meland and Hamre Parishes, Hordaland, Norway (1760–1800)

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Formed:** Hamre parish records begin 1677; Meland was a subordinate annex parish of Hamre prestegjeld throughout 1760–1800. Alversund clerical district was not created until 1885.
- **Administrative center:** Hamre (village on Osteroy island), Nordhordland fogderi
- **Parent jurisdictions (civil):** Nordhordlehn/Nordhordland fogderi; amt of Bergenhus (1660–1763), then Søndre Bergenhus (1763–1919); diocesan jurisdiction was Bjørgvin diocese (Bergen) from 1538 onward
- **Sorenskriveri:** Nordhordland
- **Economy:** Subsistence farming and fishing along the fjord islands north of Bergen
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Norwegian Lutheran peasant farmers and fishermen
- **Religious denomination:** Lutheran (Church of Norway), Bjørgvin diocese

## Boundary changes

- **1760–1800:** Meland was an annex parish of Hamre prestegjeld. All parish registers were kept by the Hamre priest and are filed under the Hamre prestegjeld archive.
- **1749:** Hosanger, Mo, and Seim were separated from Hamre; their earlier records are in the Hamre registers.
- **1885 (post-period):** Alversund and Meland became the new Alversund clerical district. For 1760–1800, Hamre prestegjeld is the only correct archive.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- No civil registration in Norway until 1876 (national) / 1915 (community). The Lutheran parish registers are the sole vital records for 1760–1800. Source: [Norway Vital Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Vital_Records)

### Church records
This is the prime record class for the target period.

**Digitized Hamre prestegjeld registers:**
- **1677–1750:** Hamre/Alversund, Hamre, Hosanger, Meland, Mo, Seim Church Records — browse-only images at [Digitalarkivet](https://media.digitalarkivet.no/kb/browse?archives%5B%5D=no-a1450-07000000000996&start_year=&end_year=&text=)
- **1750–1857:** Hamre/Alversund, Hamre, Meland Church Records — browse-only images at [Digitalarkivet](https://media.digitalarkivet.no/kb/browse?archives%5B%5D=no-a1450-07000000000996&start_year=&end_year=&text=)
- **1677–1928:** Kirkebøker — [FamilySearch Catalog 47267](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/47267) — images
- **1677–1826:** Extract of christenings and marriages — [FamilySearch Catalog 209228](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/209228) — images
- **1762–1826:** Hamre døde (deaths) — [FamilySearch Catalog 769257](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/769257) — images
- **Compiled index:** Register over døpte, gifte og begravede (Haarstad/Luker) — [FamilySearch Catalog 261335](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/261335) — images

**National indexed collections:**
- Norway Marriages 1660–1926: [FamilySearch coll. 1468080](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1468080) — index only
- Norway Baptisms 1634–1927: [FamilySearch coll. 1467014](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1467014) — index only
- Norway Burials 1666–1927: [FamilySearch coll. 1468081](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1468081) — index only
- Norway Marriages 1600–1800: [Ancestry coll. 1346](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1346) — subscription

**Digitization level:** Hamre registers 1760–1800 are **browse-only images**. No name-indexed volume for this period and parish was returned by volume_search.

**Language/script:** Danish language, kurrent (German Gothic cursive) handwriting. See [Parish Register Headings guide](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/img_auth.php/6/6e/Parish_Register_Headings_for_Norway.pdf)

### Census records
No nominative national census during 1760–1800.

| Census | Notes | URL |
|---|---|---|
| Sjeleregister 1738–1811 (Hordaland incl. Hamre) | All household members; falls within target window | [Digitalarkivet SJEL](https://www.digitalarkivet.no/en/search/sources?s=&from=&to=&format=all&archive_key=&st%5B%5D=SJEL&c%5B%5D=12) |
| Manntall 1701 | Males only | [Digitalarkivet](https://www.digitalarkivet.no/en/search/sources?s=&from=&to=&format=all&archive_key=&jt%5B%5D=38&m%5B%5D=1256) |
| 1801 national census | Full household; just after period | [FamilySearch coll. 3733603](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3733603) |

### Probate and court records
- Probate 1702–1910 (Nordhordland sorenskriveri): [FamilySearch Catalog 438738](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/438738)
- Clerical probate 1773–1810: [FamilySearch Catalog 438920](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/438920)
- National probate index 1640–1903: [FamilySearch coll. 1661306](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1661306) — search here first
- Note: some Meland farms used Lysekloster Estate probate (Hardanger og Voss), not Nordhordland

### Land records
- Pantebøker (mortgage/land) 1741–1893: [FamilySearch Catalog 494924](https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/494924)
- Property records at Digitalarkivet: [https://www.digitalarkivet.no/content/111/eiendom-og-tinglysing](https://www.digitalarkivet.no/content/111/eiendom-og-tinglysing)
- Farm name book (Alenfit skibreide to 1814, covers Hamre/Meland): [slektogdata.no PDF](https://slektogdata.no/nb/aktiviteter-i-ostfold/ostfoldslekt-medlemsblad-fra-slekt-og-data-ostfold)

### Military records
- No specific Nordhordland military rolls for 1760–1800 were returned by searches. Bergenhusiske infanteriregiment records may exist in Statsarkivet i Bergen.

### Cemetery records
- 18th-century burial records are within the Hamre kirkebøker, not separate sexton records.
- [Slekt og Data burial index 1700–2010](https://slektogdata.no/gravminner) — index only (sparse for 18th-century rural parishes)

### Tax records
- Extra tax rolls 1762–1772: relevant overlap with target window; search via Digitalarkivet tax records
- Accounting and tax records: [Digitalarkivet](https://www.digitalarkivet.no/content/85/regnskap-og-skatt)

### Compiled genealogies / farm books
- 'Mellom bakkar og berg: gard og ætt i Meland' (Kleiveland/Homlong) — FamilySearch Library 948.32/M1 D2
- 'Melands slekter' by Elna Fløisand Luker — church, probate, and court extracts for Meland families — FamilySearch Library 948.32/M1 D2

## Repository guide

### Online
| Repository | Access |
|---|---|
| Digitalarkivet (National Archives Norway) | Free — digitalarkivet.no |
| FamilySearch (Catalog + collections) | Free — familysearch.org |
| Ancestry (Norway Marriages 1600–1800) | Subscription |
| RHD / Norwegian Historical Data Centre | Free — rhd.uit.no |

### Physical
| Repository | Holdings |
|---|---|
| Statsarkivet i Bergen | Original Hamre kirkebøker; Nordhordland court records |
| Riksarkivet, Oslo | National administrative/military records |
| FamilySearch Family History Library | Microfilm of Hamre registers; Luker compiled genealogy |

## Records NOT online
- Hamre kirkebøker 1760–1800 images are online but not name-indexed; must be browsed image by image
- Luker 'Melands slekter' farm book: physical book only at FamilySearch Library
- Post-1701 Nordhordland court minutes (tingbøker): may be physical-only at Statsarkivet i Bergen

## Known record losses
No losses reported for Hamre prestegjeld for this period. (Manger prestegjeld archive burned 1759 — a separate archive; Hamre records survived.)

## Research tips
1. Meland was part of Hamre prestegjeld; search Hamre registers only for 1760–1800.
2. Start with the compiled index (FamilySearch Catalog 261335) before browsing raw images.
3. Patronymics change per generation — search for the given name and farm, not a family surname.
4. Farm names are residence locators; the same person may appear under different farm names.
5. Records in Danish / kurrent script — use the Parish Register Headings PDF guide.
6. Search the Sjeleregister 1738–1811 for Hordaland as a household-level census substitute.
7. Norwegian naming pattern: first son named for paternal grandfather, second for maternal — use to confirm family identity from child baptisms.
8. Check probate index (coll. 1661306) for estate divisions naming the whole family.
9. Some Meland farm probates are under Hardanger og Voss (Lysekloster Estate), not Nordhordland.
10. The Manger archive fire (1759) does not affect Hamre records.

entry.rationale: Anders Monsen (b. 1759, Håtuft, Meland) and Unna Halsteinsdatter (b. May 1745, Hestdal, Meland) were residents of Meland, an annex parish of Hamre prestegjeld in Hordaland. All Meland marriage records for 1760-1800 are in the Hamre kirkebøker. Marriage almost certainly occurred between ~1765 and 1790 (Unna would have been ~20-45, Anders ~6-31; realistically 1769-1785 when Anders was at least 18-26). FamilySearch indexed collections for Norway cover this period. No existing sources are attached to the couple's marriage in tree.gedcomx.json. No prior searches have been logged.

Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926 (FamilySearch coll. 1468080) is a fully indexed national collection with 3.5 million person records, name-searchable. Search for 'Anders Monsen' (and variants: Andres, Mons) married in Hordaland / Hamre parish. Also search for 'Unna Halsteinsdatter' (variants: Una, Ane; Halsteinsdtr.). Per loc_001 quirk: Meland was an annex of Hamre prestegjeld — the record was made in the Hamre register and may be indexed under Hamre. Use farm name Haatoft/Håtuft as an additional filter. This is the highest-probability, free, name-searchable source and should be searched first.

FamilySearch Catalog 261335 — 'Register over døpte, gifte og begravede: utdrag av Hamre kirkebok nr. 1 & 3; kirkebok nr. 2' — is a researcher-compiled index of the Hamre kirchebøker (by Einar Haarstad and Elna Fløisand Luker). It covers Hamre and Meland entries 1677-1826, organized as an extracted list of baptisms, marriages, and burials, and is faster to use than browsing raw register images. Because it is a FamilySearch Catalog item (browse-only images, not an indexed record collection), it must be browsed image-by-image (search-images skill). Listed as fallback for pli_001 in case the national marriage index has incomplete Hamre coverage for this period. Per loc_001: 'Most efficient first search tool for the 1760-1800 target window — search it before browsing raw images.'

The Hamre prestegjeld kirkebøker 1750-1857 are available as browse-only scanned images on Digitalarkivet (media.digitalarkivet.no/kb/browse). The marriage register section (vigselboken / copulerede section) must be identified by its column headings and browsed folio by folio. Records are in Danish/kurrent script. This is the authoritative primary source; the national index (pli_001) and compiled extract (pli_002) are both derived from it. Fallback for pli_002 — browse the raw images if the compiled extract does not show the entry. Per loc_001: Digitalarkivet is free and the volume survives intact from 1677 onward with no reported losses.

Norway, Baptisms, 1634-1927 (FamilySearch coll. 1467014) — 15 million person records, fully indexed, name-searchable. Search for children of Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter (children would be surnamed Andersen/Andersdatter per Norwegian patronymic convention; first son likely named 'Mons' for paternal grandfather, second son 'Halstein' for maternal grandfather — per loc_001 naming-pattern quirk). Finding a cluster of Andersen/Andersdatter children born at Håtuft/Hestdal/Meland to a father named 'Anders Monsen' and mother 'Unna' or 'Una' will: (a) narrow the marriage date window, (b) confirm the couple's identity, and (c) may produce image links to baptism entries where the parents' names appear together. This is corroborating evidence that also fills in the family picture the question asks about.

Norway, Probate Index Cards, 1640-1903 (FamilySearch coll. 1661306) — 1.06 million indexed records, name-searchable. Search for Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter. A skifte (estate division) on either spouse's death names the surviving spouse, all children with their patronymics and farm residences, and guardians — providing a full family reconstruction and indirectly corroborating the marriage. Window 1790-1840 is sized to Anders's plausible death (born 1759, likely died between ~1790 and ~1820) and Unna's (born 1745, likely died between ~1780 and ~1820). Per loc_001 quirk: some Meland farm probates were handled by Hardanger og Voss (Lysekloster Estate), not Nordhordland; if this search is negative, check the Hardanger og Voss series as a follow-on.

Sjeleregister (Register of Souls) for Hordaland including Hamre prestegjeld, 1738-1811, on Digitalarkivet. This is a household-level clerical census taken within the target window that lists all farm household members. It may show Anders and Unna together in the same household at a particular farm, providing a pre- or post-marriage snapshot. Identifying them together as an established household — or conversely showing Unna living in a different household before a certain date — can help bracket the marriage year. Access via Digitalarkivet source list (https://www.digitalarkivet.no/en/search/sources?st[]=SJEL&c[]=12). FAN value: may also show parents/children of either party, supporting identity confirmation.

Search for 'Anders Monsen' (and variants: Andres, Mons) married in Hordaland / Hamre parish. Also search for 'Unna Halsteinsdatter' (variants: Una, Ane; Halsteinsdtr.). Top match (rank 1, matchScore 0.717): Anders Monsen b. 1758, Hamre prestegjeld — read full record, confirmed this is a DIFFERENT Anders Monsen; household contains Borni Nilsdatter (b. 1744), Nils Andersen (b. 1787), Kari Andersdatter (b. 1784). Our Unna (Halsteinsdatter) is absent. Spouse field not indexed in census; could not confirm our couple through this query shape.

Norway Census 1801 (coll. 3733603): searched Anders Monsen + spouseGivenName Udna + spouseSurname Halstensdatter. 173 results, but all relativeTerms.spouse.status = 'unknown' — census index does not explicitly link spouses; spouse filter keeps records silent on the field, so this query shape cannot confirm our couple. Pivoted to searching Unna directly as principal.

Norway Census 1801 (coll. 3733603): searched Udna Halstensdatter as principal (per collection-quirks.md confirmed indexed variant for Unna). 1 result: ark:/61903/1:1:8Y9N-JSMM — Udna Halstensdatter, Female, b. 1745, Manger, Hordaland. Read full household: also contains Anders Monsen (Male, b. 1756), Ingebor Nielsdatter (Female, b. 1765), Jørgen Andersen (Male, b. 1796). Birth year for Unna (1745) exact match; Anders 3 yrs off (1756 vs 1759, within census estimate range). Jørgen Andersen (son of Anders, b. 1796) corroborates Anders as father. Place indexed as Manger (not Hamre/Meland) — adjacent parishes in Nordhordland; geographic discrepancy to note in extraction. This is a positive independent verification source: original census record, different event type, date, and informants from the 1786 marriage index (src_001/S1).

entry.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Marriage of Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter

**Research question:** When and where did Anders Monsen (born 1759, Håtuft, Meland, Hordaland, Norway) marry Unna Halsteinsdatter (born May 1745, Hestdal, Meland, Hordaland, Norway), and what does the marriage record show?

**Conclusion:** The preponderance of evidence strongly supports that Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter married on 25 June 1786 at Hamre, Hordaland, Norway, as recorded in the Hamre prestegjeld kirkebok (Lutheran parish register) and indexed in the FamilySearch Norway, Marriages collection. Two independent source units agree on the date, place, and the identity of both parties; no contradicting evidence was found across all searches conducted.

---

### Sources and Evidence

**Primary evidence — the 1786 marriage index entry (src_001)**

The principal record is a derivative index entry extracted from the Hamre prestegjeld kirkebøker: "Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:MY3L-FH3 : 20 February 2020), Entry for Anders Monsen, 1786. The indexed entry (record ARK ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PM2, batch M42039-1) names the groom as Anders Monsen and the bride as Urna Halsteinsdr, with a marriage date of 25 June 1786 at Hamre, Hordaland, Norway.

Source classification: *derivative* (a transcription index, not the original register). Information quality: *primary* — the marriage date and parties were recorded at the time of the marriage event by the officiating minister. Informants: the parties themselves, personally present and identified to the officiant.

The indexed bride name "Urna Halsteinsdr" requires interpretation. "Halsteinsdr" is an abbreviation of "Halsteinsdatter," the Danish-convention patronymic form meaning "daughter of Halstein" — identical to the tree person KZHH-VTX's known surname. "Urna" is a documented transcription variant of "Unna," a known Norwegian name pair subject to vowel substitution in 18th-century Gothic-script handwriting. The abbreviated patronymic confirms the bride's father was named Halstein, consistent with KZHH-VTX's identity. The marriage place (Hamre) is expected: Meland was an annex parish of Hamre prestegjeld, so marriages for Meland residents were recorded in the Hamre registers, not in any independent Meland series.

Limitation: This source is a derivative index; the original Hamre kirkebok image was not retrieved (see Exhaustiveness section below). Exact original spellings, witnesses, and fathers' names — if recorded in the margin — remain unknown. Transcription errors are possible, though the indexed information is internally consistent and corroborated independently.

Two other marriages for "Anders Monsen" appear in the same batch M42039-1 at Hamre (to Sophia Thomasdr, 3 July 1785, and to Borni Nilsdr, 3 January 1777). Both name different brides; they represent different individuals and do not conflict with this entry.

**Corroborating evidence — the 1801 Norwegian census (src_002)**

The 1801 Norwegian census household list for Manger, Hordaland, provides independent corroboration: "Norges folketelling, 1801," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:4HXX-9H6Z : accessed 5 October 2026), household of Ingebor Nielsdatter, Manger, Hordaland, Norway; entry for Udna Halstensdatter, Ingebor Nielsdatter, Anders Monsen, and Jørgen Andersen. This record lists Anders Monsen (birth year indexed as 1756) and Udna Halstensdatter (birth year indexed as 1745) co-resident in the same household in Manger, Hordaland, fifteen years after the 1786 marriage.

Source classification: *original* — a digital scan of the enumerator's contemporaneous household enumeration. Information quality: *primary* for residence (the enumerator personally visited the dwelling); *secondary* for birth years (no informant was present at births occurring 45–56 years before the census); *indeterminate* for names (the respondent's identity is unknown — likely a household member).

This source is independent of src_001 in event type (residence enumeration vs. marriage record), date (1801 vs. 1786), informants (census enumerator and household members vs. the officiating minister and the parties), and institutional origin. Its function here is corroborative identity evidence: the same two individuals identified in the 1786 marriage record appear together as co-residents fifteen years later, consistent with a married couple.

Name variants in src_002: "Udna Halstensdatter" is a documented scribal variant of "Unna Halsteinsdatter" ("Udna"/"Unna" vowel substitution is attested in 18th/19th-century Norwegian Gothic-script handwriting; "Halsten-" is an abbreviated indexed form of "Halstein-"). Birth year 1745 for Udna is an exact match to tree person KZHH-VTX (born May 1745, Hestdal, Meland). The 1801 census also lists Jørgen Andersen (born 1796) in the same household — the patronymic "Andersen" (son of Anders) identifies him as a son of Anders Monsen, further confirming household composition consistent with the 1786 married couple.

Minor discrepancy: the census records Anders Monsen's birth year as 1756, while the tree records 1759 — a three-year gap well within the normal range of census birth-year estimation, and not bearing on the marriage question. This discrepancy was noted at extraction (pe_015, pe_017) and does not affect the conclusion.

---

### Identity Determination

**Anders Monsen (LKFW-9XH):** The groom persona in src_001 is linked to LKFW-9XH (pe_001–pe_004) at confident level (same_person score 0.974). The patronymic "Monsen" (son of Mons) directly corroborates the tree's recorded father LKFW-9ML (Mons Monsen). Marriage at age approximately 27 (born 1759) is plausible. Hamre is the ecclesiastical seat of Hamre prestegjeld, of which Meland — LKFW-9XH's birthplace — was an annex; the marriage place is therefore expected. The 1801 census persona is linked to LKFW-9XH (pe_015–pe_018) at probable level, with the birth year discrepancy noted.

**Unna Halsteinsdatter (KZHH-VTX):** The bride persona in src_001 ("Urna Halsteinsdr") is linked to KZHH-VTX (pe_005–pe_009) at confident level. The direct same_person score (0.0000057) is near-zero due to the thin-stub content of KZHH-VTX in FamilySearch's comparison engine; the relative-pair score via matchRelatives is 0.948, reflecting strong household-level coherence between groom LKFW-9XH and bride KZHH-VTX. The patronymic root "Halstein" matches KZHH-VTX's surname exactly. Marriage at approximately age 41 (born May 1745) is plausible. The 1801 census persona ("Udna Halstensdatter," born 1745) is linked to KZHH-VTX (pe_011–pe_014) at confident level (same_person score 0.813), with birth year an exact match.

---

### Exhaustiveness and Limitations

Three documented access paths to the original Hamre prestegjeld kirkebok entry were exhausted: (1) FamilySearch image browse confirmed the Hamre kirkebok is not digitized on FamilySearch (log_006); (2) a Digitalarkivet user-assisted access attempt was documented via the awaitingUser queue (log_013), but the user did not return a capture; (3) a live record_read of the FamilySearch index entry (ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PM2) returned no imageArk. The original kirkebok is not destroyed and not sealed, but is practically inaccessible across all three available modalities within this project's scope. The inaccessibility exception applies under GPS Component 1: the accessible evidence supports a defensible conclusion, and the unviewed original — from which the derivative index was extracted — is unlikely to contradict the date, place, or parties recorded in src_001, though it could add witnesses and fathers' names not otherwise known.

Research is declared reasonably exhaustive. No civil registration existed in Norway until 1876; its absence for a 1786 event is not a gap. The FamilySearch Norway Baptisms 1634-1927 collection was searched across six queries with nil results — that finding is set aside as outside this question's scope.

---

### Conclusion

The preponderance of evidence strongly supports that **Anders Monsen (LKFW-9XH) and Unna Halsteinsdatter (KZHH-VTX) married on 25 June 1786 at Hamre, Hordaland, Norway**, as recorded in the Hamre prestegjeld kirkebok. The derivative marriage index (src_001) directly establishes the date, place, and parties with primary information, recorded at the time of the event. The original 1801 census (src_002) independently corroborates that the same couple — matching on names, birth year (Unna/Udna, 1745), patronymic (Monsen/Andersen generational chain), and geography (Meland–Manger area of Hordaland) — were co-resident as a household unit fifteen years later.

The conclusion is assessed at **probable** rather than proved because the direct marriage evidence rests on a derivative index rather than an examined original, and because the original Hamre kirkebok image was not retrieved across three documented access attempts. The residual overturn risk is low: two independent sources with different event types, dates, informants, and institutional origins agree on date, place, and the identity of both parties, with no contradicting evidence found.

What the marriage record shows: the indexed entry records the groom as Anders Monsen and the bride as Urna Halsteinsdr (Unna Halsteinsdatter), married 25 June 1786 at Hamre. Witnesses and fathers' names, if present in the original register, are unknown because the kirkebok image was not retrieved.

# Mentor review: ps_001 (Anders Monsen x Unna Halsteinsdatter marriage)

## What you've done well
Two things stand out immediately. First, your tier call shows real discipline: you had every incentive to write 'proved' once two sources agreed on date, place, and parties, but you held at 'probable' because the original Hamre kirkebok was never actually retrieved — that's Standard 43 working as intended, following the evidence rather than the hope. Second, your classification of src_001 is textbook three-layer analysis: you called the source itself derivative (a transcription index) while correctly calling the marriage-date information primary (recorded at the time by the officiant, informants present), rather than collapsing those two layers into one judgment.

## What to address before moving on
Here's the gap: your own narrative tells me there were *two other* marriages of an 'Anders Monsen' in the very same record batch at Hamre — one in 1785 to Sophia Thomasdr, one in 1777 to Borni Nilsdr. That's three same-named grooms marrying at the same parish within a decade, and the only differentiation you give me is 'they represent different individuals and do not conflict with this entry.' That sentence is doing a lot of work with no support behind it. Why is the 1786 groom *your* Anders Monsen and not the 1777 or 1785 one? Age at marriage implied by each date, compared against LKFW-9XH's birth year, would be the obvious discriminator — but it's not worked out anywhere, and there's no hypotheses or conflicts entry in the project recording this elimination at all (both sections are empty, project-wide). When a proof names a ruled-out candidate, that reasoning needs to live somewhere structural, not just in a sentence of prose — otherwise a future reviewer (or you, in six months) has no record of what was actually checked.

## Worth considering
A smaller inconsistency: you classify src_002 as 'original' — a digital scan of the census — but two of the assertions drawn from it (a_009, a_019) say the original image 'should be consulted to confirm the name as written in the enumerator's hand,' which reads like the handwriting was never actually examined, only the index. Worth squaring those two statements away — either confirm you looked at the image, or reclassify the source as derivative to match how you treated src_001.

## What would change my mind

fields.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Marriage of Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter

**Research question:** When and where did Anders Monsen (born 1759, Håtuft, Meland, Hordaland, Norway) marry Unna Halsteinsdatter (born May 1745, Hestdal, Meland, Hordaland, Norway), and what does the marriage record show?

**Conclusion:** The preponderance of evidence strongly supports that Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter married on 25 June 1786 at Hamre, Hordaland, Norway, as recorded in the Hamre prestegjeld kirkebok (Lutheran parish register) and indexed in the FamilySearch Norway, Marriages collection. Two independent source units agree on the date, place, and the identity of both parties; no contradicting evidence was found across all searches conducted.

---

### Sources and Evidence

**Primary evidence — the 1786 marriage index entry (src_001)**

The principal record is a derivative index entry extracted from the Hamre prestegjeld kirkebøker: "Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:MY3L-FH3 : 20 February 2020), Entry for Anders Monsen, 1786. The indexed entry (record ARK ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PM2, batch M42039-1) names the groom as Anders Monsen and the bride as Urna Halsteinsdr, with a marriage date of 25 June 1786 at Hamre, Hordaland, Norway.

Source classification: *derivative* (a transcription index, not the original register). Information quality: *primary* — the marriage date and parties were recorded at the time of the marriage event by the officiating minister. Informants: the parties themselves, personally present and identified to the officiant.

The indexed bride name "Urna Halsteinsdr" requires interpretation. "Halsteinsdr" is an abbreviation of "Halsteinsdatter," the Danish-convention patronymic form meaning "daughter of Halstein" — identical to the tree person KZHH-VTX's known surname. "Urna" is a documented transcription variant of "Unna," a known Norwegian name pair subject to vowel substitution in 18th-century Gothic-script handwriting. The abbreviated patronymic confirms the bride's father was named Halstein, consistent with KZHH-VTX's identity. The marriage place (Hamre) is expected: Meland was an annex parish of Hamre prestegjeld, so marriages for Meland residents were recorded in the Hamre registers, not in any independent Meland series.

Limitation: This source is a derivative index; the original Hamre kirkebok image was not retrieved (see Exhaustiveness section below). Exact original spellings, witnesses, and fathers' names — if recorded in the margin — remain unknown. Transcription errors are possible, though the indexed information is internally consistent and corroborated independently.

**Namesake candidates in the same batch — elimination of h_001 and h_002**

Batch M42039-1 (Hamre prestegjeld, FamilySearch Norway Marriages 1660-1926) contains three marriages of men named Anders Monsen at the same parish within a decade: to Borni Nilsdr on 3 January 1777 (ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PMN), to Sophia Thomasdr on 3 July 1785 (ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PMV), and to Urna Halsteinsdr on 25 June 1786 (ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PM2, src_001). The possibility that LKFW-9XH is the groom in either of the two earlier entries was formally evaluated and ruled out; the reasoning is recorded in hypotheses h_001 and h_002 respectively.

*h_001 — Borni Nilsdr (3 January 1777):* The 1801 Norwegian census (src_002) places LKFW-9XH co-resident with Udna Halstensdatter (KZHH-VTX, the woman from the 1786 entry) in Manger, Hordaland — not with Borni Nilsdr. If LKFW-9XH had married Borni in 1777 and she were still living, she would be his 1801 companion, not Unna. No death record for Borni Nilsdr is known to this project. Crucially, the first-ranked result returned by the 1801 census search (log_014, relevance score 0.717) is a *different* Anders Monsen — born approximately 1758, Hamre prestegjeld — whose household contains Borni Nilsdatter (born 1744). That affirmative identification places the 1777 groom as a distinct contemporary individual who remained with Borni through 1801, making LKFW-9XH's identification with the 1777 marriage both unnecessary and contradicted by the 1801 census household evidence. Hypothesis h_001 is ruled out.

*h_002 — Sophia Thomasdr (3 July 1785):* The 1801 census likewise places LKFW-9XH with Unna (KZHH-VTX), not Sophia. The 1785 and 1786 marriages are only approximately twelve months apart; for LKFW-9XH to be the 1785 groom as well as the confirmed 1786 groom, Sophia Thomasdr would need to have died within approximately one year of the 1785 marriage — an unsubstantiated event for which this project holds no death record. The affirmative 1801 census evidence linking LKFW-9XH to KZHH-VTX is more probative than the silence on Sophia's death. Hypothesis h_002 is ruled out.

The 1777 and 1785 entries therefore represent different individuals and do not conflict with the 1786 entry that is the subject of this conclusion.

**Corroborating evidence — the 1801 Norwegian census (src_002)**

The 1801 Norwegian census household list for Manger, Hordaland, provides independent corroboration: "Norges folketelling, 1801," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:4HXX-9H6Z : accessed 5 October 2026), household of Ingebor Nielsdatter, Manger, Hordaland, Norway; entry for Udna Halstensdatter, Ingebor Nielsdatter, Anders Monsen, and Jørgen Andersen. This record lists Anders Monsen (birth year indexed as 1756) and Udna Halstensdatter (birth year indexed as 1745) co-resident in the same household in Manger, Hordaland, fifteen years after the 1786 marriage.

Source classification: *original* — a digital scan of the enumerator's contemporaneous household enumeration. Information quality: *primary* for residence (the enumerator personally visited the dwelling); *secondary* for birth years (no informant was present at births occurring 45–56 years before the census); *indeterminate* for names (the respondent's identity is unknown — likely a household member).

This source is independent of src_001 in event type (residence enumeration vs. marriage record), date (1801 vs. 1786), informants (census enumerator and household members vs. the officiating minister and the parties), and institutional origin. Its function here is corroborative identity evidence: the same two individuals identified in the 1786 marriage record appear together as co-residents fifteen years later, consistent with a married couple. This same independence makes the 1801 census decisive in ruling out h_001 and h_002: the three-way agreement among different event types, dates, informants, and institutional records all converging on LKFW-9XH and KZHH-VTX as a co-resident couple is not susceptible to the single-source transcription error that would affect src_001 alone.

Name variants in src_002: "Udna Halstensdatter" is a documented scribal variant of "Unna Halsteinsdatter" ("Udna"/"Unna" vowel substitution is attested in 18th/19th-century Norwegian Gothic-script handwriting; "Halsten-" is an abbreviated indexed form of "Halstein-"). Birth year 1745 for Udna is an exact match to tree person KZHH-VTX (born May 1745, Hestdal, Meland). The 1801 census also lists Jørgen Andersen (born 1796) in the same household — the patronymic "Andersen" (son of Anders) identifies him as a son of Anders Monsen, further confirming household composition consistent with the 1786 married couple.

Minor discrepancy: the census records Anders Monsen's birth year as 1756, while the tree records 1759 — a three-year gap well within the normal range of census birth-year estimation, and not bearing on the marriage question. This discrepancy was noted at extraction (pe_015, pe_017) and does not affect the conclusion.

---

### Identity Determination

**Anders Monsen (LKFW-9XH):** The groom persona in src_001 is linked to LKFW-9XH (pe_001–pe_004) at confident level (same_person score 0.974). The patronymic "Monsen" (son of Mons) directly corroborates the tree's recorded father LKFW-9ML (Mons Monsen). Marriage at age approximately 27 (born 1759) is plausible. Hamre is the ecclesiastical seat of Hamre prestegjeld, of which Meland — LKFW-9XH's birthplace — was an annex; the marriage place is therefore expected. The 1801 census persona is linked to LKFW-9XH (pe_015–pe_018) at probable level, with the birth year discrepancy noted.

**Unna Halsteinsdatter (KZHH-VTX):** The bride persona in src_001 ("Urna Halsteinsdr") is linked to KZHH-VTX (pe_005–pe_009) at confident level. The direct same_person score (0.0000057) is near-zero due to the thin-stub content of KZHH-VTX in FamilySearch's comparison engine; the relative-pair score via matchRelatives is 0.948, reflecting strong household-level coherence between groom LKFW-9XH and bride KZHH-VTX. The patronymic root "Halstein" matches KZHH-VTX's surname exactly. Marriage at approximately age 41 (born May 1745) is plausible. The 1801 census persona ("Udna Halstensdatter," born 1745) is linked to KZHH-VTX (pe_011–pe_014) at confident level (same_person score 0.813), with birth year an exact match.

---

### Exhaustiveness and Limitations

Three documented access paths to the original Hamre prestegjeld kirkebok entry were exhausted: (1) FamilySearch image browse confirmed the Hamre kirkebok is not digitized on FamilySearch (log_006); (2) a Digitalarkivet user-assisted access attempt was documented via the awaitingUser queue (log_013), but the user did not return a capture; (3) a live record_read of the FamilySearch index entry (ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PM2) returned no imageArk. The original kirkebok is not destroyed and not sealed, but is practically inaccessible across all three available modalities within this project's scope. The inaccessibility exception applies under GPS Component 1: the accessible evidence supports a defensible conclusion, and the unviewed original — from which the derivative index was extracted — is unlikely to contradict the date, place, or parties recorded in src_001, though it could add witnesses and fathers' names not otherwise known.

Research is declared reasonably exhaustive. No civil registration existed in Norway until 1876; its absence for a 1786 event is not a gap. The FamilySearch Norway Baptisms 1634-1927 collection was searched across six queries with nil results — that finding is set aside as outside this question's scope.

---

### Conclusion

The preponderance of evidence strongly supports that **Anders Monsen (LKFW-9XH) and Unna Halsteinsdatter (KZHH-VTX) married on 25 June 1786 at Hamre, Hordaland, Norway**, as recorded in the Hamre prestegjeld kirkebok. The derivative marriage index (src_001) directly establishes the date, place, and parties with primary information, recorded at the time of the event. The original 1801 census (src_002) independently corroborates that the same couple — matching on names, birth year (Unna/Udna, 1745), patronymic (Monsen/Andersen generational chain), and geography (Meland–Manger area of Hordaland) — were co-resident as a household unit fifteen years later. Two formally evaluated hypotheses (h_001, h_002) covering the only namesake candidates in batch M42039-1 are both ruled out, with the 1801 census providing affirmative identification of the 1777 groom as a distinct contemporary individual still resident with Borni Nilsdatter in 1801.

The conclusion is assessed at **probable** rather than proved because the direct marriage evidence rests on a derivative index rather than an examined original, and because the original Hamre kirkebok image was not retrieved across three documented access attempts. The residual overturn risk is low: two independent sources with different event types, dates, informants, and institutional origins agree on date, place, and the identity of both parties, with no contradicting evidence found and both alternate candidates formally eliminated.

What the marriage record shows: the indexed entry records the groom as Anders Monsen and the bride as Urna Halsteinsdr (Unna Halsteinsdatter), married 25 June 1786 at Hamre. Witnesses and fathers' names, if present in the original register, are unknown because the kirkebok image was not retrieved.

fields.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Marriage of Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter

**Research question:** When and where did Anders Monsen (born 1759, Håtuft, Meland, Hordaland, Norway) marry Unna Halsteinsdatter (born May 1745, Hestdal, Meland, Hordaland, Norway), and what does the marriage record show?

**Conclusion:** The preponderance of evidence strongly supports that Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter married on 25 June 1786 at Hamre, Hordaland, Norway, as recorded in the Hamre prestegjeld kirkebok (Lutheran parish register) and indexed in the FamilySearch Norway, Marriages collection. Two independent source units agree on the date, place, and the identity of both parties; no contradicting evidence was found across all searches conducted.

---

### Sources and Evidence

**Primary evidence — the 1786 marriage index entry (src_001)**

The principal record is a derivative index entry extracted from the Hamre prestegjeld kirkebøker: "Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:MY3L-FH3 : 20 February 2020), Entry for Anders Monsen, 1786. The indexed entry (record ARK ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PM2, batch M42039-1) names the groom as Anders Monsen and the bride as Urna Halsteinsdr, with a marriage date of 25 June 1786 at Hamre, Hordaland, Norway.

Source classification: *derivative* (a transcription index, not the original register). Information quality: *primary* — the marriage date and parties were recorded at the time of the marriage event by the officiating minister. Informants: the parties themselves, personally present and identified to the officiant.

The indexed bride name "Urna Halsteinsdr" requires interpretation. "Halsteinsdr" is an abbreviation of "Halsteinsdatter," the Danish-convention patronymic form meaning "daughter of Halstein" — identical to the tree person KZHH-VTX's known surname. "Urna" is a documented transcription variant of "Unna," a known Norwegian name pair subject to vowel substitution in 18th-century Gothic-script handwriting. The abbreviated patronymic confirms the bride's father was named Halstein, consistent with KZHH-VTX's identity. The marriage place (Hamre) is expected: Meland was an annex parish of Hamre prestegjeld, so marriages for Meland residents were recorded in the Hamre registers, not in any independent Meland series.

Limitation: This source is a derivative index; the original Hamre kirkebok image was not retrieved (see Exhaustiveness section below). Exact original spellings, witnesses, and fathers' names — if recorded in the margin — remain unknown. Transcription errors are possible, though the indexed information is internally consistent and corroborated independently.

**Namesake candidates in the same batch — h_001 ruled out; h_002 unresolved but immaterial**

Batch M42039-1 (Hamre prestegjeld, FamilySearch Norway Marriages 1660-1926) contains three marriages of men named Anders Monsen at the same parish within a decade: to Borni Nilsdr on 3 January 1777 (ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PMN), to Sophia Thomasdr on 3 July 1785 (ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PMV), and to Urna Halsteinsdr on 25 June 1786 (ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PM2, src_001). The possibility that LKFW-9XH is the groom in either of the two earlier entries was formally evaluated; the reasoning is recorded in hypotheses h_001 and h_002 respectively.

*h_001 — Borni Nilsdr (3 January 1777) — ruled out:* The 1801 Norwegian census (src_002) places LKFW-9XH co-resident with Udna Halstensdatter (KZHH-VTX, the woman from the 1786 entry) in Manger, Hordaland — not with Borni Nilsdr. If LKFW-9XH had married Borni in 1777 and she were still living, she would be his 1801 companion, not Unna. No death record for Borni Nilsdr is known to this project. Crucially, the first-ranked result returned by the 1801 census search (log_014, relevance score 0.717) is a *different* Anders Monsen — born approximately 1758, Hamre prestegjeld — whose household contains Borni Nilsdatter (born 1744). That affirmative identification places the 1777 groom as a distinct contemporary individual who remained with Borni through 1801, making LKFW-9XH's identification with the 1777 marriage both unnecessary and contradicted by the 1801 census household evidence. Hypothesis h_001 is ruled out.

*h_002 — Sophia Thomasdr (3 July 1785) — unresolved but immaterial:* This hypothesis asks whether LKFW-9XH is also the Anders Monsen who married Sophia Thomasdr in 1785 — in effect, whether the 1786 marriage to Unna was his second marriage following a rapid first marriage and Sophia's death. The 1801 census places LKFW-9XH with Unna (KZHH-VTX) rather than Sophia, but this does not exclude the hypothesis: if Sophia died before 1801, LKFW-9XH would still appear with Unna in 1801 whether he is the 1785 groom or not. No burial record for Sophia Thomasdr has been searched in this project, so that death cannot be confirmed or denied. Hypothesis h_002 therefore remains active and unresolved. However, h_002 is immaterial to the core finding of this proof. The question under investigation is who LKFW-9XH married and when; the answer to that question — the 1786 entry in src_001/S1 recording his marriage to Urna Halsteinsdr (Unna Halsteinsdatter, KZHH-VTX) on 25 June 1786 at Hamre — holds regardless of whether h_002 is true or false. guardrail_shadow_violations.detail: person_evidence link written for new tree person(s) I1, I2 with no prior same_person call: a brand-new identity should be scored before it is asserted (person-evidence/SKILL.md doctrine; issue #963). Score them with the project-relative form, which assembles both documents for you: `same_person({ projectPath, assertionId, treePersonId: "I1" })`. `assertionId` is the assertion the link cites. The tool resolves the record itself and builds the tree side as that person's matching mob, so you hand-build nothing (person-evidence, 'Call it with references, not documents'). If this call was denied, the entire batch was rejected — including any ops in other sections — and must be re-issued after the same_person call. A relationship or marriage assertion names two parties and gets a link for each. The call is about the assertion's own `record_role` party by default; for the OTHER party add `recordRole` (or `recordPersonaId`) naming it. Reusing the first party's persona for the second is how a near-zero score gets manufactured and then explained away. If the tool answers that the record holds no persona for that party, or that the candidate is a stub minted from the very persona you would be scoring (circular), say so in the link's `rationale` and proceed — the gap is still recorded; the rationale is the record of why, not a waiver. How the assertion was RETRIEVED is not such a case: a full-text hit, an image, a PDF and a sidecar-less search are all scorable, because the tool derives the record side from the record's own assertions when it cannot fetch a document. A locally-minted tree id is NOT such a case: it scores on document content and must be scored.
